newsitem.title: UK: Middle East crude tanker rates hold, UKC slips.
newsitem.headline: Middle East crude tanker rates hold, UKC slips.

text.p: World crude tanker rates held steady on Wednesday in the key Middle East lifting sector, but some slippage was seen in a quiet UK/cont market.
Chartering was slow in the Mediterranean, but rates were holding while West Africa saw fair busy and firm charter rates.
In the Middle East VLCCs travelling to Japan were able to command W75, well ahead of the W60 or so same size tankers can command to Singapore, shipping brokers said.
They said 250,000 tonnes looking for carriage westwards would be able to secure transport in the high W50s.
Dealers said the healthy fixing of the last few days had drawn out tonnage, but that a bounce higher in rates was not anticipated.

The UK/continent market was still in a patch of the doldrums with rates on benchmark 80,000 tonners making cross cont trips slipping to W100-105 from the W110 seen earlier in the week. Shipbrokers said it was the usual case of too many ships, not enough trips.

In the West African theatre of operations both VLCCs and suezmaxes were able to find work. Shippers said VLCCs to the U.S. were taking around W65 with suezmaxes (130,000 tonnes) settling for W20 less.
Mediterranean aframax business continued to be sparse, but for the moment rates were holding up around W120 for typical cross Med trips.
"There is not a lot going on at the moment, so we could see rates start to ease," said one shipbroker.
In the Caribbean up U.S coast market a plethora of fixtures were seen with typical 70,000 tonners attracting W145 or so.
